And whether you disclose» that is, make manifest «what is in yourselves» of evil and of equity «or conceal it» that is, keep it secret «Allah will bring you to account for it» on the Day of Resurrection «so He forgives whom He wills» [whom He wills] forgiveness for «and punishes whom He wills» [whom He wills] to punish «and Allah is powerful over everything» (Q. 2:284) and that includes bringing you to account and requiting you; when it came down, Abū Bakr came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him: ⟨If Allah takes us to account for what is in our souls, then we perish; we have no capacity for this.⟩ The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Do you wish to say what the people of the two Books before you said: We have heard and we have disobeyed?⟩ Abū Bakr said: ⟨No, but we have no capacity for this. If Allah takes us to account for what is in our souls, there is no deliverance at all.⟩ so there came down «Allah does not burden»

«a soul beyond its capacity» (Q. 2:286) [44] — the āya that follows. «The Messenger has believed» [that is,] Muhammad «in what has been sent down to him from his Lord» of the Qurʾan «and the believers» [this is] coordinated with it «each one» of them «has believed in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers» (Q. 2:285)

They say: «We make no distinction between any of His messengers» so as to believe in some and disbelieve in others, as the Jews and the Christians did. «And they said: We have heard» [that is,] what we were commanded — a hearing of acceptance «and we have obeyed. Your forgiveness» we ask You for Your forgiveness «our Lord, and to You is the return» (Q. 2:285) When the āya before it came down, the believers complained of the whispering [of the soul], and being brought to account for it weighed heavily upon them. And so there came down: «Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity» that is, [beyond] what its power can encompass «To it belongs what it has earned» (Q. 2:286)

of good «and against it is what it has acquired» of evil «Our Lord» [that is,] say: Our Lord «do not take us to task» with punishment «if we forget or err» (Q. 2:286) [that is,] we have abandoned what is right, [not] deliberately, as You took to task those before us for it. And Allah has lifted that

from this community, as has come in the hadith. So his asking [for this] is an acknowledgement of Allah’s favour. «Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden» a matter whose carrying weighs heavily on us «as You laid it upon those before us» the Children of Israel: the killing of the self, since whoever wished to repent would kill himself; and the handing over of a quarter of one’s wealth, for the alms-tax was a quarter of their wealth; and the cutting away of the place [touched by] impurity «Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength for» of obligations and affliction «and pardon us» efface our sins «and forgive us and have mercy on us» mercy is something more than forgiveness «You are our Protector» our Master and the One who manages our affairs «so help us against the disbelieving people» (Q. 2:286) by establishing the proof and by victory in fighting them, for it belongs to a protector to help those under his protection against enemies, and in the hadith: ⟨When this āya came down and he ﷺ recited it, he was told after every phrase: I have done [it].⟩ His supplication was answered.
Sūrat Āl ʿImrān
Medinan. Two hundred āyāt , or [two hundred] less one āya .

«By Allah’s Name: The Entirely Merciful, The Especially Merciful» «Alif Lām Mīm» (Q. 3:1) Allah knows best what He intends by it. The right course in interpreting it is: Allah knows best what He intends. It came down concerning the disputation of the Messenger ﷺ with the delegation of the Christians of Najrān.

Sixty riders came from the Christians of Najrān. Among them was the king, among them the head of the bishops, and among them the greatest of their merchants, their rich man — they are the lords to whose word [the rest] defer. They came to the Prophet ﷺ disputing with him about the affair of ʿĪsā. At one time they would say: ʿĪsā is Allah, because he gives life to the dead and heals the one born blind and the leper, and creates from clay the likeness of a bird — so he is Allah. At another time they would say: ʿĪsā is a son to Allah, because he has no father. Have you seen a child with no father? Since he had no father, we know that Allah is his father. At another time they would say: the third of three…

Have you not read the word of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, ‘We did’ and ‘We said’? Had He been alone, He would have said ‘I said’ and ‘I did’. [47] The Prophet ﷺ said to them: ⟨Do you know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Living and does not die?⟩ They said: Yes.

He said: ⟨And does death come to ʿĪsā?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes.⟩ He said: ⟨Do you not know that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is able to form people in the wombs, and that ʿĪsā has nothing of that?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes indeed.⟩ He said: ⟨Do you not know that a child must resemble his father, and Allah is the Living, the Self-Subsisting, whom no slumber takes nor sleep, living, who never dies, while ʿĪsā — his mother carried him as women carry, and she bore him as women bear, and she suckled him as women suckle, and he used to eat and drink and relieve himself?⟩ They said: ⟨Yes indeed.⟩ He said: ⟨You know that ʿĪsā — the Christians claimed that they killed him, and he was powerless to defend himself, while Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is living, abiding.⟩ They said: ⟨Yes.⟩ And so there came seventy āyāt from

the beginning of this sura, concerning that disputation, making clear the confirmation of the Prophet ﷺ and his agreement with the truth. [48] «Allah — there is no deity but He, The Living, The Self-Subsisting» (Q. 3:2) Allah, the one who deserves worship; there is no object of worship in truth other than Him. And He is «The Living» — the everlasting; «The Self-Subsisting» — the one who undertakes the governance of His creation perpetually. ʿĪsā is not like that. «And He sent down upon you» O Muhammad «the Book» the Qurʾan «with the truth, confirming what was before it» (Q. 3:3) That the Qurʾan came down upon Muhammad — in this is the strongest proof for Muhammad ﷺ of his truthfulness in what he said. «and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before, as guidance» — guides out of error — «for mankind» (Q. 3:3–4) because if they acknowledge that Allah sent down the Torah and the Gospel, they cannot deny that Allah sent down the Qurʾan upon Muhammad. Either they disbelieve in all the prophets and all the books, and so disbelieve in the Qurʾan; but if they affirm the truth of one prophet among the prophets, or one book among the books, then they cannot declare false

Muhammad or the Qurʾan, for they have no argument. The prophets came with books from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and what strengthened them, so that we accepted that this came from Allah, were the miracles; and Muhammad came with a book from Allah and came with dazzling miracles. So how can one believe in a prophet and disbelieve in Muhammad ﷺ, when he has miracles they do not have, and when he claimed nothing but a book that came to him from Allah, Blessed and Exalted? For this reason He informed them that it is He who sent down this Book, just as He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before. «and He sent down the Furqān» (Q. 3:4) meaning the books that distinguish truth from falsehood, or the miracles, in all three. So either one affirms all of them or one disbelieves in all of them: may Allah protect us from that. «Those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs will have a severe punishment; and Allah is Mighty» prevailing in His affair, so nothing prevents Him from carrying out His promise and His threat «Possessor of retribution» (Q. 3:4) a severe punishment for whoever disobeys Him «Allah: nothing is hidden from Him» that exists «in the earth or in the heaven» (Q. 3:5) because of His knowledge of what occurs in the world, universal and particular «He it is who forms you in the wombs however He wills» as the Prophet ﷺ mentioned: maleness and femaleness, whiteness and blackness «there is no deity but He, the Mighty, the Wise» (Q. 3:6) in what He makes. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s belly for forty days as a drop, and forty days as a clot, and forty days as a morsel of flesh; then the spirit is breathed into him.⟩ And in another narration: ⟨When there falls⟩

The drop of fluid in the mother’s womb: the angel asks, Is he wretched or felicitous? And he is answered: wretched, or felicitous. Rich or poor? And he is answered: rich or poor. What is his deed, and what is his term? These four — the pen has dried upon them. This is an instruction to the angel of what had already preceded in the Tablet; otherwise, this had already preceded before the child’s descent into its mother’s womb. «And He it is who sent down upon you the Book; of it are determinate verses — they are the mother of the Book» (Q. 3:7) Allah is He who sent down this Qurʾan upon Muhammad. In it are determinate verses, clear in their signification; they are the foundation of the Book, and from them the rulings were derived. «and others ambiguous» (Q. 3:7) — their meanings are not understood, like the openings of the suras. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, described the Qurʾan as being entirely muḥkam : «its verses have been made determinate» (Q. 11:1). So it became entirely muḥkam . This is because it is without precedent in its composition, its meanings, its eloquence and its rhetoric. And He described the Qurʾan as being entirely mutashābih : «Allah has sent down the best of discourse, a Book of resembling parts, paired» (Q. 39:23). That is because of the resemblance of one part of it to another. And He described the Qurʾan as being of two parts: in it there is muḥkam and mutashābih . The muḥkam is what is clear in its signification, and the mutashābih is what is not understood in its meaning, like the openings of the suras, and the attributes of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and the like. The Qurʾan, then, falls into four parts. One part is clear with a manifest clarity, so that everyone who knows Arabic understands its meaning when he hears it, such as «Say: He is Allah, One» (Q. 112:1) — every Arab knows the meaning of «He is Allah, One» — and this is the greater part of the Qurʾan. One part contains obscure meanings and requires deep competence in Arabic, in grammar, in morphology and in rhetoric, and for this reason it requires an exegete to explain it. One part none knows except those firmly rooted in knowledge. And one part none knows except Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and that is the mutashābih , such as the mention of a hand for Allah, Blessed and Exalted. He said that He has a hand, and He said that He has two hands: «rather, His two hands»

«are outstretched» (Q. 5:64) — and both of them are a right hand. [50] This a human being does not understand: the two hands, each one of them is a right hand. And He mentioned that He has hands, many hands: «and the heaven — We built it with hands» (Q. 51:47). If we have recourse to taʾwīl , as those who practise it hold, and say that the hand is power, the naming [text uncertain] refutes this, because power is not put into the dual, much less into the plural. So the attributes of Allah with which He described Himself: we believe in them according to what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, intends by them. This is what is correct. He mentioned that He has a face, and that He has a hand; He mentioned that He has a foot; He mentioned that He descends; He mentioned that He istawā . All of these are sound meanings which Allah knows and we do not know. The chief qadi in the Hijaz questioned me — they affirm direction, they say that Allah is seated upon the Throne, in these very words, we seek refuge with Allah; they do not say mustawin , they say seated upon the Throne — he followed me in the Hijaz until he sat down at my side and began to question me. He said to me: Whoever does not hold that [Allah] is seated above the Throne, his faith is deficient, or he is not a believer. «The Merciful — upon the Throne He settled» (Q. 20:5). And in the hadith: ⟨Where was our Lord before He created the heavens and the earth? Cloud above cloud, and Allah above that.⟩ [51] And the hadith: ⟨Allah created seven heavens and chose the seventh.⟩ [52] He recited all of this to me, so I said to him: I hold that

Allah mentioned for Himself a Throne and a Footstool, and He mentioned that He istawā upon His Throne, and the Throne is hidden from us. But He also mentioned that He has a House, and here we are at His House now. He mentioned that He has a she-camel: have we ever seen Him ride a she-camel? He said: No.

I said: «the she-camel of Allah and her drink» (Q. 91:13) — whose is this she-camel? This is the House of Allah: if we enter it, do we find Him in it or not? He said: We do not find Him in it. I said: If, when we enter His House, we do not find Him there — and the norm is that a man is found in his house — then it is possible that His Throne too, if we come to it, we will not find Him upon it. He said: What are we to do with this hadith: ⟨Our Lord descends every night, when the first third of the night has passed, and says: Is there any petitioner, that I may give to him? Is there any caller, that I may answer him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness, that I may forgive him?⟩ [53] This descent is proof that He is above. I said to him: Yes, He descends every night, and we believe that. But this Qurʾan says that Allah sent down to us eight kinds of livestock: of camels two, of cattle two, of sheep two, of goats two. These are eight that Allah reported He sent down to us from heaven. Every day we see a she-camel giving birth to a camel, and we see a cow giving birth to a cow, and we see a ewe giving birth to a ewe, and a she-goat giving birth to a she-goat. How did these descend from heaven, when we are watching their mothers give birth to them? He said: We do not know the reality

How did it descend from heaven? I said: if we do not understand the descent of the animals, how are we to understand the descent of the Master, Mighty and Exalted? He fell silent. As for al-mutashābih [the ambiguous], the sound position concerning it is the position of al-Shāfiʿī: ⟨We believe in what Allah said according to what Allah intended, and we believe in the speech of the Messenger of Allah according to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended.⟩ «As for those in whose hearts there is deviation» an inclination [away from the truth] «they follow what is ambiguous in it, seeking discord» because of their ignorance of their own falling into the ambiguities «and seeking its interpretation» its exegesis «And none knows its interpretation» its exegesis «except Allah» alone «and those firmly rooted in knowledge say: We believe in it» (Q. 3:7) Or: none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge — none knows it except Allah and those firmly rooted; or: none knows it except Allah, and those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ’We believe in it.’ [This is] a mark of knowledge as well. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Learn knowledge, for learning it for Allah’s sake is fear [of Him], seeking it is worship, investigating it is⟩ jihad ⟨, and teaching [it] to one who does not know it is alms — since it is the markers of the licit and the illicit. Knowledge is the intimate in desolation, the companion in solitude, the one who converses in seclusion. By it Allah raises people up until He makes them leaders and imams whose deeds are taken as a pattern⟩
⟨and their words⟩
[54] ⟨and they become intercessors with Allah on the Day of Resurrection.⟩ [55] [printed line out of order:] «All» of the muḥkam and the mutashābih «they say: We believe in it» (Q. 3:7)

in the mutashābih «All» of the muḥkam and the mutashābih «is from our Lord. And none takes heed» takes admonition «except those possessed of understanding» the possessors of intellects. «Our Lord, do not cause our hearts to deviate» make them incline away from the truth by seeking an interpretation of it that does not befit us «after You have guided us» You have directed us «and grant us from Your presence» from You «a mercy» a setting [of us] aright «Truly You are the Bestower. Our Lord, truly You are the gatherer of mankind» You will gather them «for a day» on a day «in which there is no doubt» that is the Day of Resurrection, and You will requite them for their deeds «Truly Allah does not break the appointed promise» (Q. 3:8–9) His promise of the resurrection on it. In this there is a turning away from the [second-person] address [ iltifāt ], and it may be part of His own speech, Exalted. The purpose of the supplication in these terms is to show that their concern is the matter of the hereafter; and for that reason they asked for steadfastness in guidance, that they might attain its reward. The two Shaykhs transmitted from ʿAʾisha, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with her, who said: ⟨The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this āya:⟩ «He it is who sent down upon you the Book; in it are decisive verses» (Q. 3:7) ⟨to the end of it, and he said: ’If you see those who follow what is ambiguous in it, those are the ones Allah has named, so beware of them.’⟩ [56] And al-Ṭabarānī transmitted in al-Kabīr from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: ⟨I fear for my community nothing but three traits⟩ — and he mentioned among them: ⟨that the Book be opened to them, and the believer takes it seeking its interpretation, while none knows its interpretation except Allah⟩ «and those firmly rooted in»

«knowledge say: We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord. And none take heed but those possessed of understanding» (Q. 3:7) «Those who disbelieve: there will not avail» that is, ward off «them, their wealth or their children, against Allah» against His punishment «anything; and they are the fuel of the Fire» (Q. 3:10) the fuel of the Fire is that with which it is kindled, their way, that is, their custom [was] «like the way of the folk of Pharaoh» like the custom of the folk of Pharaoh «and those before them» of the nations, such as ʿĀd and Thamūd «they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them» (Q. 3:11) that is, destroyed them

«for their sins» on account of their sins «and Allah is severe in punishment» (Q. 3:11) It was revealed when the Prophet ﷺ commanded the Jews to [accept] Islam on his return from Badr, and they said to him: ⟨Do not let it delude you that you have fought a band of Quraysh, raw youths who do [not] know fighting. If you confront us, you will know that we are the men and we are the champions.⟩ [58] So it was revealed. «Say» O Muhammad «to those who disbelieve» of the Jews «you will be overcome» (Q. 3:12) by killing and captivity and the levying of the jizya — and that has come to pass.

This is a miracle. «and you will be gathered to Hell» and so enter it «and wretched is the resting place» (Q. 3:12) the bed, In addressing the Prophet ﷺ, they said that his fighting was against Quraysh, and that they are callow and know nothing of war, so that it gives no ground for boasting; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, mentioned that expedition, namely the battle of Badr «there has been for you a sign» a lesson «in two companies» two groups «that met» on the day of Badr, for battle «one company fighting in Allah’s path» (Q. 3:13) that is, in obedience to Him
and they are the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions. They were three hundred and thirteen men, and with them two horses. [59]

and six coats of mail and eight swords; most of them were on foot. This is the army of the Prophet ﷺ. «and another, disbelieving — you see them as twice their number» — that is, the Muslims more numerous than the disbelievers. And they were about a thousand: Quraysh a thousand, or nine hundred. [60] And Allah mentioned that at the beginning of the affair He makes them few in your eyes and makes you few in their eyes, as comes in Sūrat al-Anfāl — this is at the beginning — and at the end He made the disbelievers look upon the Muslims as though they were two thousand, so that their fear of them would increase. Is this not lesson enough? A company of brave men, a thousand, every one of them trained for war, with a sword, and a horse, and provision enough; and three hundred who had no weapons but eight swords, and no mounts but two horses, the horse of al-Zubayr and the horse of al-Miqdād, only these. So they met, and they feared them — that is, those of the thousand [were the ones who feared] — until they saw them as twice their number, «to the eye’s seeing» — and this was direct witnessing: Allah created that, so they saw them plainly, as though they were two thousand. «And Allah strengthens with His help whom He wills. In that there is a lesson for those possessed of sight.» (Q. 3:13) This is the Battle of Badr. It took place in Shawwāl in the second year of the Hijra, a year after the Hijra. The Messenger ﷺ invoked [Allah] against Quraysh: ⟨O Allah, make it years upon them like the years of my brother Yūsuf.⟩ [61] Then the drought fell, until they went hungry, until they ate apes and ate dogs. So they gathered their wealth and their stores and sent their lesser king, Abū Sufyān. He went to Syria and bought for them a great store of provisions. And when

he returned, the Prophet ﷺ saw in a dream that Allah had given him one of the two parties: Abū Jahl, with him the army, and Abū Sufyān, with him the caravan. Allah promised him one of the two parties, as will come in Sūrat [illegible: الكبيل] . So they gathered. As for the caravan, they fled and saved themselves and reached the Hijaz; and as for the war-party, they went out [illegible: بالز] armed to the teeth in weapons, and they came to Badr. In this there was a sign, that is, a lesson, because the Prophet ﷺ announced that they would be victorious, and he announced the places where the people would fall: so-and-so is struck down here, and so-and-so is struck down here, and [illegible: وقيله] is struck down here, to the last of them; and the matter fell out as he had said. So they met, and the Muslims overcame them, and they took captive from among them [illegible: مسعو] chiefs from among their chiefs, among them al-ʿAbbās b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. This is a lesson for whoever takes a lesson. More of [illegible: العدي] will come
in Sūrat al-Anfāl.

«The love of desires has been made alluring to people» — what the soul craves and is drawn to. Allah made them alluring as a trial, or Satan [did]. In this āya He mentioned seven things that a human being loves, seven things in which a human being’s desires lie; love is gathered in them. And you know that a person loves a thing and does not love to love it, as a Muslim loves something forbidden — so then, that is, he does not love to love it; and he loves a thing that he loves to love and in which his desire does not lie; and he loves a thing that he loves to love and in which his desire does lie — this is the stronger. All of them came together in the āya : the love of desires. He mentioned that they are desires made alluring to them and that they loved them. «of women» — when a man comes of age, the first thing he attaches himself to is to find a wife who suits him. «and sons» — when he has found a wife, he loves that Allah provide him with children. «and heaped-up hoards of gold and silver» — and when he has found women and sons, he loves to find much gold and silver. As for gold, its own word makes you renounce it: al-dhahab is from al-dhahāb , going away; so everything you own of gold must go away. And silver, al-fiḍḍa , is from al-faḍḍ , which is scattering: everything you own of silver must be scattered. Women and sons and gold and silver. «and branded horses» — the steeds; they are called khayl for their khuyalāʾ [their vainglorious bearing]. «and cattle» — camels and cows and sheep and goats. «and tilled land» — cultivation. «That is the enjoyment of the life of this world» — all these things are goods enjoyed in this world,

then it perishes. «and with Allah is the best of returns» (Q. 3:14) That is the goodly place of return, which is the Garden, with Allah, Blessed and Exalted; so one should desire it and nothing else. ʿAli, may Allah ennoble his face, said: ⟨Man’s appetites are in women, food, drink, clothing, and mounts.⟩ He said: ⟨The best food is honey, and it is only the excrement of a fly; the best drink is water, in which people, beasts, livestock and wild animals are all alike; women are only a urinary passage within a urinary passage; the best of mounts are horses, and upon them men are killed; and the finest clothing is silk, which is only the excrement of a worm.⟩ None of this deserves attention. Attention belongs to what is with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and that is attained only by obeying Him, by carrying out His command and avoiding what He forbids. O Allah, bless our master Muhammad.

المسمى بالعرائس

قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِے مِن لَّدُنكَ  ·  اِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ اُ۬لدُّعَآءِۖ فَنَادَتْهُ اُ۬لْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ  ·  وَهُوَ قَآئِمࣱ يُصَلِّے فِے اِ۬لْمِحْرَابِ  ·  وَسَيِّدا  ·  وَحَصُوراً  ·  وَامْرَأَتِ عَافِر  ·  كَذَّلِكَ

قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلاَّ تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ  ·  ثَلَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ  ·  بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالابْكَرِ وَ  ·  وَإِذْ قَالَتِ اِ۬لْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اَ۬للَّهَ اَ۪صْطَف۪يٰكِ  ·  وَطَهَرَ  ·  وَاصْطَفِيَكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَآءِ الْعَلَمِينَ
وَاسْجُدِے وَارْكَعِے مَعَ اَ۬لرَّٰكِعِينَۖ
وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمُۥٓ إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمُۥٓ  ·  أَيَّهُمْ يَكْفَلَ مَرْيَمٌ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمُ  إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ

إِسْمَهُ الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى إِبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهاً  ·  والآخِرَةِ  ·  وَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ  ·  وَيُكَلِّمُ اُ۬لنَّاسَ فِے اِ۬لْمَهْدِ  ·  وَكَهْلًا  ·  وَمِ الصَّلِحِيرٌ قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَىٰ يَكُونُ لِي وَلَدْ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرّ بتزويج قَالَ  ·  اللَّهُ يَخْلُوُ مَا يَشَآءُ إِذَا قَضِىّ أَمْراً فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ و كُن فَيَكُونٌ  ·  وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْرِيَةَ وَالانجِيلَ  ·  وَرَسُولاً اِلَيٰ بَنِےٓ إِسْرَآءِيلَ
أَنِّے قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةࣲ
بَأَنمُغُ جِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طِيِراً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَأَبْرِئُ  ·  اُ۬لَاكْمَهَ وَالَابْرَصَ وَأُحْيِ اِ۬لْمَوْت۪يٰ بِإِذْنِ اِ۬للَّهِۖ
وَجِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْۖ

فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأطِيعُونَ  ·  عِيسِى مِنْهُمْ الْكَهْرَ  ·  قَالَ مَنَ انصَارِى  ·  وَاتَّبعْنَا الرَّسُولَ  ·  وَمَكَرَ أللَّه  ·  وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَكِرِينَ  ·  إِذْ قَالَ اَ۬للَّهُ يَٰعِيس۪يٰٓ إِنِّے مُتَوَفِّيكَ  ·  وَرَابِعُكَ إِلَىِّ  ·  وَمُطَقِرْكَ  ·  إِلَى يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَمَةٌ ثُمَّ إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ  ·  وَالآخِرَةِ  ·  وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَۖ وَأَمَّا اَ۬لذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ اُ۬لصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَنُوَفِّيهِمُۥٓ أُجُورَهُمْۖ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ اُ۬لظَّٰلِمِينَۖ ذَٰلِكَ  ·  نَتْلُوهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الايَتِ وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ  ·  إنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسِى  ·  عِندَ اَ۬للَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَۖ  ·  خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابࣲ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُنۖ  ·  جَيَكُونُ  ·  أُلْحَقُّ مِن رَبِّكَ  ·  فَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ اَ۬لْمُمْتَرِينَۖ فَمَنْ حَآجَّكَ  ·  جِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَكَمِنَ ألْعِلْمِ  ·  ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ  ·  فَنَجْعَل لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَذِبِينُ
فَإِنَّ اَ۬للَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَۖ  ·  فُلْ يَأَهْلَ الْكِتَبِ  ·  تَعَالَوا اِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَآءٍ

أَلَّ نَعْبُدَ إِلَّ اللَّهَ وَلَا نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْاً وَلَا يَتَّخِذَّ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضاً أَرْبَاباً صِ دُودِ اللَّه بَإِن تَوَلَّوْا أعرضوا عن التوحيد جَفُولُوا  ·  إشْهَدْواْ بِأَنَّا مَسْلِمُونَ  ·  يَٰٓأَهْلَ اَ۬لْكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِےٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَۖ  ·  أَوَلا تَعْفِلُونُ  ·  هَآنتُمْ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ حَٰجَجْتُمْ فِيمَا لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلْمࣱ  ·  وَأَنتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ  ·  مَا كَانَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ يَهُودِيّاࣰ وَلَا نَصْرَانِيّاࣰ وَلَٰكِن كَانَ حَنِيفاࣰ مُّسْلِماࣰۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ اَ۬لْمُشْرِكِينَۖ إِنَّ أَوْلَي اَ۬لنَّاسِ  ·  وَهَذَا الَيَة  ·  يَٰٓأَهْلَ اَ۬لْكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ
وَالذِين ءَامَنُوا  ·  وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ اُ۬لْمُومِنِينَۖ وَدَّت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنَ اَهْلِ اِ۬لْكِتَٰبِ لَوْ يُضِلُّونَكُمْۖ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمْ
وَقَالَت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنَ اَهْلِ اِ۬لْكِتَٰبِ
ءَاخِرَهُ لَعَلَّهَمْ  ·  يَرْجِعُونَ
وَلا تُومِنُوا
وَاللَّهُ وَسِعٌ

يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ، مَنْ يَشَآءٌ وَاللّهُ ذُو اُلْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمُ وَمِنَ آهْلِ الْكِتَبِ مَنِ تَامَنْهُ بِقنطارٍ  ·  إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَآئِماࣰۖ  ·  وَاِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُواْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا مِي الأُمِّيِّيَ  ·  سَبِيلٌ  ·  وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ

وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ  ·  بَل۪يٰ مَنَ اَوْف۪يٰ بِعَهْدِهِۦ  ·  وَاتَّفِى  ·  فَإِنَّ اَ۬للَّهَ يُحِبُّ اُ۬لْمُتَّقِينَۖ إِنَّ اَ۬لذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ  ·  بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ  ·  وَأَيْمَنِهِمْ  ·  لَمَناً فَلِيلًا  ·  اوْلِئِكَ لا خَلَّقَ

لَهُمْ فِے اِ۬لَاخِرَةِ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اُ۬للَّهُ  ·  وَلَا يَنظُرْ إِلَيْهِمْ  ·  يَلْوُنَ أَلْسِنَتَهُم بِالْكِتَبِ لِتَحْسِبُوهُ مِنَ الْكِتَبِ  ·  وَمَا هُوَ مِنَ الْكِتَٰبِ وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ  ·  لِبَشَرٍ آَنْ يُوتِيَهُ اللَّهُ الْكِتَبَ وَالْحُكْمَ  ·  وَالنُّبُوٓءَةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُواْ عِبَاداࣰ لِّے مِن دُونِ اِ۬للَّهِ وَلَٰكِن  ·  بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
الْكِتَبَ وَبِمَا كُنتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ  ·  وَلَا يَامُرُكُمُۥٓ أَن تَتَّخِذُواْ اُ۬لْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ وَالنَّبِيٓـِٕۧنَ أَرْبَاباًۖ

ايَامُرُكُم بِالْكُفْرِ بَعْدَ إِذَ آنتُم مُسْلِمُونَ  ·  وَإِذَ اَخَذَ اَ۬للَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ اَ۬لنَّبِيٓـِٕۧنَ  ·  لَمَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم مِّن كِتَٰبࣲ وَحِكْمَةࣲ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولࣱ مُّصَدِّقࣱ لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ  ·  لَتُومِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُ
آقْرَرْتُمْ  ·  وَأَخَذْتُمْ  ·  عَلَى ذَٰلِكُمُو إِصْرِى
قَالُوٓاْ أَقْرَرْنَاۖ قَالَ فَاشْهَدُواْ  ·  وَأَنَا مَعَكْم مِنَ الشَّهِدِينَ
فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ اُ۬لْفَٰسِقُونَۖ أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اِ۬للَّهِ تَبْغُونَ وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ  ·  وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونْ

وَمَنْ يَّبْتَغِ غَيْرَ اَ۬لِاسْلَٰمِ دِيناࣰ فَلَنْ يُّقْبَلَ مِنْهُۖ وَهُوَ فِے اِ۬لَاخِرَةِ مِنَ اَ۬لْخَٰسِرِينَۖ كَيْفَ يَهْدِے اِ۬للَّهُ  ·  وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِے اِ۬لْقَوْمَ اَ۬لظَّٰلِمِينَۖ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمُۥٓ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اَ۬للَّهِ وَالْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا
رَحِيٌّ  ·  الَّ ألذِينَ كَجَرْوا

قَمَّ إَزْدَادُواْ كَفْرا  ·  وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ اُ۬لضَّآلُّونَۖ إِنَّ اَ۬لذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمْ كُفَّارࣱ فَلَنْ يُّقْبَلَ مِنَ اَحَدِهِم مِّلْءُ اُ۬لَارْضِ ذَهَباࣰ  ·  وَلَوِ اِ۪فْتَد۪يٰ بِهِۦٓۖ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ اَلِيمࣱۖ  ·  وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَۖ
«Say» — O Muhammad, to your people — «shall I announce to you» — shall I inform you — «of something better than that» — the aforementioned among

the desires. «For those who guarded against» — polytheism — «with their Lord are gardens beneath which rivers run, abiding» — decreed to abide forever — «therein» — once they have entered them — «and purified spouses» — purified of menstruation and of whatever else is found repugnant — «and good pleasure from Allah» — abundant good pleasure — «and Allah is seeing» — knowing — «of the servants» (Q. 3:15), and so He requites each of them according to his deed. He told us of what has been made alluring to people among the desires of this world, and He called the servants to desire what is better than that, which is working for the hereafter.

Whoever works for the hereafter enters the Garden and finds in it what no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, and what has never occurred to the heart of any human being. Greater than all of that is the good pleasure of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, after which there is no displeasure. «And good pleasure from Allah is greater» (Q. 9:72). When a person enters the Garden and sees the blessings in it, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Shall I give you more? They say: Yes — and is there anything beyond this? He says: My good pleasure — I settle it upon you, and I shall never be displeased with you thereafter. As for the people of the Garden, of everything they have found in the Garden of blessings, the greatest of it in their eyes is their [illegible: كوكُم]

they are pleased with Allah and Allah is pleased with them. «Return to your Lord, well pleased and well pleasing» (Q. 89:28). This is better than this world and everything in it. Paradise is two paradises: a sensory paradise and a spiritual paradise. The spiritual paradise is knowledge of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and whoever enters it does not long for the paradise still to come. Among people there is the one who works out of fear of the Fire, the one who works out of desire for the Garden, and the one who works for the face of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, because He deserves servitude from the servant; those are the free. «Those who say: Our Lord, we have believed» — we have affirmed the truth of You and of Your messenger — «so forgive us our sins and shield us from the punishment of the Fire» (Q. 3:16). These servants address their Lord in intimate speech: Our Lord, we have believed — faith has come about in us, so forgive us our sins. This proves that whoever believes in Allah has thereby merited forgiveness. «The patient» (Q. 3:17) — I praise the patient. Patience has three ranks: patience under affliction — whoever is patient under affliction is raised three hundred degrees, the distance between two degrees being as the distance between heaven and earth; and patience in obedience — whoever is patient in obedience is raised six hundred degrees, the distance between two degrees being as the distance between heaven and earth; and patience in abstaining from disobedience — whoever is patient in abstaining from disobedience is raised nine hundred degrees, the distance between two degrees being as the distance between heaven and earth.

⟨O people of the Garden. And they say: We are at Your service, our Lord, and at Your good pleasure. So He says: Are you content? And they say: Why should we not be content, when You have given us what You have given to none of Your creation? So He says: I shall give you something better than that. They said: Lord, and what thing is better than that? So He says: I settle My good pleasure upon you, and I shall never be displeased with you thereafter.⟩

Lesser patience is patience under affliction, middling patience is patience in obedience, and great patience is [illegible: الصن] from disobedience. Patience in obedience: many Muslims comply with the commands, and that comes about only through patience. Patience in abstaining from disobedience is the furthest degree; none attain it but the righteous among the servants of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Many Muslims comply with the commands; as for avoiding the prohibitions, none have attained it but the righteous, and it is the highest degree of patience. Patience is half of faith. «And the truthful» — in faith: those who were truthful in saying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and who were truthful in their deed. Truthfulness in speech is that your deed accord with your word. Truthfulness in deed is that a man stand firm in doing good, keep to it steadily, and remain resolved upon it always, nothing turning him back from it. «And the devoutly obedient» — those obedient to Allah — «and those who spend» — those who give alms — «and those who seek forgiveness» — of Allah, by saying: O Allah, forgive us — «in the last hours before dawn» (Q. 3:17) — the final parts of the night; they were singled out [illegible: بالمكّ] because they are the time of heedlessness and of the pleasure of sleep. [2] He mentioned the attributes — «the patient, and the truthful, and the devoutly obedient, and those who spend, and those who seek forgiveness in the last hours before dawn» — with the wāw . This shows that whoever is characterized by a single one of these attributes is among the righteous, the patient. The station of patience: whoever is granted it is among the righteous. And truthfulness is a station. «And the devoutly obedient and those who spend» . Had He said: the patient, the truthful, the devoutly obedient, those who spend, those who seek forgiveness, we would have needed to combine the attributes before we could be among the righteous; but since He joined them with the wāw , this entails that every one of these attributes obliges the servant to be among the righteous. The awliyāʾ of the shariʿa : everyone characterized by one of the attributes the Qurʾan praises is among the awliyāʾ . This is the lesser walāya .

1 — The singling out of this time is attested in the hadith: ⟨Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven, when the last third of the night remains, and says: Who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me, that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?⟩

And the greater [ walāya ] is the knowers [of Allah]: whoever has known Allah with the maʿrifa of direct vision. «Those who seek forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours» (Q. 3:17) — the last portions of the night — on account of the hadith of the descent. The Messenger ﷺ says: ⟨Allah grants respite until half the night has passed⟩ — and in [another] transmission, ⟨until a third of the night remains⟩ — two transmissions — ⟨then He descends to the lowest heaven and says: Is there any supplicant, that I may answer him? Is there any petitioner, that I may give to him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness, that I may forgive him?⟩ [3] This is the hadith of the descent, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has no direction, no place and no time. This descent is an expression for the Lord’s turning with His mercy toward His servants. The descent of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wherever it is mentioned in the hadith, means His turning toward the servant. When He turns toward you, He has descended to you. So in the hadith of ʿArafāt: that Allah descends at ʿArafa and says, addressing the pilgrims: ⟨You have come dishevelled and dust-stained. Depart forgiven. I have accepted the good deeds from you, and I have accepted the doers of good among you, and I have bestowed the evildoers upon the doers of good. Depart forgiven, and your liabilities [are discharged] from My treasuries, not from your good deeds.⟩ [4] This is evidence that the hour of answering is in every night, and that it falls in the last part of the night. For this reason it is encouraged that the servant[’s] work be in the night, that he defer it to the last portion of it. The Sufis say: Be a star; and if you cannot, be a moon; and if

you cannot, be a sun. Be a star: be one who devotes himself to worship the whole night through, just as the star passes the whole night [illegible: سانا] . And if you cannot, be a moon — that is, you devote yourself to worship during a portion of the night. The moon courses through one part of the night and is absent during another part. And if you are not able, be a sun: worship in the daytime. Every lover loves khalwa with his beloved. And amid the night are the prayers of the khalawāt . Ibn ʿUmar used to say to his servant-boy: ⟨Have you reached the time before dawn?⟩ — have you entered into the saḥar ? If he said no, he would rise and pray; and if he said yes, he would sit and seek Allah’s forgiveness, interpreting this āya . «Allah bears witness that there is no god but He» (Q. 3:18) — it was sent down when the Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: Bring us the greatest testimony in the Qurʾan. He said: «Allah bears witness» — He has made clear to His creation by proofs and signs — «that there is no god» — there is no object of worship in existence, by right, other than He — «but He» — and the angels bore witness to that: «and the angels» — they bore witness by affirmation — «and those possessed of knowledge» — they too bore witness by affirmation. Those possessed of knowledge are of the prophets and the believers, by conviction and by utterance — «maintaining» — the governance of the things He has made, in the state of His maintaining the governance of the things He has made — «with justice» — with equity — «there is no god but He» — He repeated it for emphasis — «the Mighty» — in His dominion — «the Wise» (Q. 3:18) — in His making. «Truly the religion» — the one approved — «in Allah’s sight» — Blessed and Exalted — is «Islam» (Q. 3:19) — the Law with which the messengers were sent, founded upon tawḥīd . So Islam is Allah’s religion, the one He has approved for the whole of His creation, from the beginning of time to the end of time; and though they differed over some kinds of acts of worship, they agreed upon faith in Allah alone, upon magnifying Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and upon compassion toward His creation. «Truly the religion in Allah’s sight is Islam» (Q. 3:19): Wāʾil related from ʿAbdallāh b. Masʿūd that the Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Whoever recites:⟩ «Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels, and those possessed of knowledge, maintaining with justice; there is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise. Truly the religion in Allah’s sight is Islam» (Q. 3:18–19) ⟨and [then says]: ‘And I deposit this testimony with You, so that it is a deposit of mine with You, my Lord’ — he will be summoned on the Day of Resurrection and the Lord will say: ‘My servant has a covenant with Me, and I am the worthiest of those who fulfil a covenant⟩

⟨Admit him to the Garden — and he enters the Garden.⟩ Ghālib b. Qaḥṭān said: ⟨I was travelling, and I lodged with al-Aʿmash. When the time of the last watch of the night came, I heard him repeating this āya and saying: It is a deposit of mine with You, my Lord. So I said [to myself]: Something has reached him concerning this āya. I had resolved to set out, so much so that my baggage went off with the caravan. When he had prayed the dawn prayer I said to him: I heard you repeating this āya — has anything reached you concerning it? He said: I will not tell you until you stay with me a full year. He said: Write down this day, such-and-such a day of the year, and I shall be at your door —⟩ until the year was complete. When the year was complete, he told him this hadith of Wāʾil from Ibn Masʿūd: that whoever recites this āya and makes it a deposit with Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will come on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will call out to him before all the witnesses: ⟨You have a covenant with Me, and I am the most worthy of those who fulfil a covenant, so enter the Garden.⟩ «And those who were given the Book did not differ» the Jews and the Christians — in religion, in that some affirmed [Allah’s] oneness and some disbelieved «except after the knowledge had come to them» [the knowledge] of [Allah’s] oneness «out of rivalry» out of envy, on the part of the disbelievers «among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in Allah’s signs — Allah is swift in reckoning» (Q. 3:19) in requiting him «If they dispute with you» the disbelievers contend with you, Muhammad, about religion «then say: I have submitted my face to Allah» I have yielded to Him «and so has whoever follows me. And say to those who were given the Book» the Jews and the Christians «and to the unlettered» the idolaters of the Arabs «Have you submitted?» [meaning] submit «Then if they submit, they have been guided» out of error «but if they turn away» from Islam «your duty is only the conveying» the delivery [of the message] «and Allah sees the servants» (Q. 3:20) so He will requite them for their deeds This was before the command to fight. «Those who disbelieve in Allah’s signs and kill the prophets without»

«right» wrongfully «and kill those who enjoin equity» with justice «from among the people» (Q. 3:21) they are the Jews. It is reported that they killed forty-three prophets, and a hundred and seventy of [illegible: من غادهم] forbade them, and they killed them [illegible: من يوروا]

«Give them tidings» — inform them — «of a painful punishment» (Q. 3:21) — that is, one that causes pain — and mentioning glad tidings here is tahakkum [mockery]. «Those are the ones whose deeds have come to nothing» — have been nullified; [their deeds being] whatever good they did, such as alms and keeping the ties of kinship — «in this world and the Hereafter» (Q. 3:22). So if

reckoning of them, for want of their condition «and they have no helpers» (Q. 3:22) who would ward off the punishment «Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book» (Q. 3:23) The occasion for the revelation of this āya is that two persons among the Jews committed fornication, and they were of their notables. The Torah contained the ruling of stoning, but they had altered and changed it: when a notable fornicated they flogged him, and when a lowly man fornicated they stoned him. So when these two persons fornicated, and they were of their notables, they said: we shall go to the Prophet ﷺ to find a dispensation with him. When they told him the matter, he said: ⟨The Book of Allah is stoning.⟩ They said: ⟨No — you have wronged us, Abū al-Qāsim; stoning is not incumbent upon us.⟩ He said: ⟨Stoning is incumbent. Stoning is in the Book of Allah and in the Torah. Bring the Torah.⟩ They said: ⟨The Torah does not contain stoning.⟩ So they brought the Torah, and ʿAbd Allah b. Ṣūriyā set about reading until he reached the verse of stoning; he placed his finger on the word ’stoning’ and read what came after it. ʿAbd Allah b. Salām was present, and he knew the Torah by heart; he lifted his hand and read the verse of stoning, and the Prophet ﷺ had the two of them stoned. So this āya was revealed concerning them: «Have you not seen those who were given a portion» a share «of the Book» the Torah «they are called to the Book of Allah that it may judge between them, then a party of them turns away, and they are averse» (Q. 3:23) from accepting its judgement «That» the turning away «is because they said: the Fire will not touch us except for a number of days» (Q. 3:24) That is because they are deluded by their own lies — that they will not enter the Fire, or that if they enter it they will stay a number of days, because they are Allah’s children and His beloved — the span of their forefathers’ worship of the calf. «and what they used to fabricate has deluded them in their religion» they fabricated things. Their chiefs invented lies for them, and they held those lies to be true and went astray through them, until they forgot the Book of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And this — though it was revealed concerning the Jews

— applies to many of the Muslims. The Muslim must have hope and fear. Hope is that which action accompanies; otherwise it is delusion. A person acts, and does his work well, and hopes in Allah, Blessed and Exalted, for His mercy, and fears on account of the badness of his deeds; so he is on a straight path so long as fear and hope contend over his heart. And when his appointed time draws near, he gives the weight to the side of hope, on account of the hadith: ⟨I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me what he will.⟩ Whoever claims that he hopes in Allah, Blessed and Exalted, while he abandons the works of good, is deluded; this is not hope, it is only a wish. «and what they used to fabricate has deluded them in their religion» (Q. 3:24) They used to say: we are of the progeny of Ibrāhīm, and Ibrāhīm is the intimate friend of Allah; we are of the progeny of ʿUzayr, and ʿUzayr is the son of Allah; we are Allah’s children and His beloved; so it is impossible that we should ever be among the people of the Fire.

A human being does not torment his own sons, nor does he torment those dear to him. This is self-delusion on their part, and a fabrication. Just as the leaders of the Jews fabricated lies to which the common people of the Jews clung until they went astray, so too many of the chiefs of the Muslims have fabricated lies by which they have deluded a body of the Muslims until they lost the way. It is related that a servant entered the Fire and remained

in it for a time. Then a voice was heard: ⟨O Compassionate One, O Bestower, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour.⟩ The angels said: [illegible: هذه الكلي لي الندار يارب؟] He said: ⟨Bring out the one who uttered it.⟩ So they brought him out and set him before Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and he had turned black and had been burned until he became charcoal. Then al-Ḥaqq called him to account a second time, and he deserved the Fire. He said: ⟨Return him to the Fire.⟩ So they went back with him to the Fire, while he kept turning to the right and to the left. The Lord said to the angels: ⟨Bring him back.⟩ So they brought him back. He said: ⟨Why do you keep turning toward Me?⟩ He said: ⟨My Lord, I disobeyed You, and my hope in You was not cut off; and You called me to account and I incurred the Fire, and my hope was not cut off; and You admitted me into the Fire, and my hope was not cut off; and You set me before You, and my hope was not cut off; and You commanded that I be returned to the Fire — and until now my hope in You has not been cut off, my Lord.⟩ So He said: ⟨Admit him to the Garden.⟩ And they admitted him
to the Garden.

«So how will it be when We gather them for a day» — on a day — «there is no doubt» — no uncertainty — «about it» — and it is the Day of Resurrection — «and every soul will be paid in full» — from among the People of the Book and others — the recompense of «what it earned» — what it did of good and of evil — «and they»

— that is, the people — «will not be wronged» (Q. 3:25) — by the diminishing of a good deed or the adding of an evil one. There is no wrongdoing on the Day of Resurrection. «Whoever does the weight of a speck of good will see it, and whoever does the weight of a speck of evil will see it» (Q. 99:7–8). «Say: O Allah, Possessor of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will» (Q. 3:26). This āya was sent down on the day of the Trench, when the idolaters gathered from every quarter and came to the city

on account of the severity of hunger, [by way of] strengthening. The Sufis have said that he feared his spirituality would overcome his corporeality and that he would then vanish from among us. In any case, he went down into the trench and took up the pickaxe, after he had performed the ablution and had poured his ablution water over the rocks. He struck, and a third of the rock broke apart, and a great light shone, as though a large lamp had been lit in a dark house. He said: ⟨Allah is greater.⟩ He struck a second time and a third, and it became scattered dust. Salmān said: ⟨We have seen a wonder:⟩

⟨Every time you struck with the pickaxe we saw a great light, as though a lamp had been lit in a dark house.⟩ He said: Did you see what Salmān saw? They said: Yes. He said: ⟨When I struck the first time, I looked toward the villages of al-Ḥīra, and I was given the good news that my Companions would possess them. The second time I saw the lands of the Byzantines — I saw the red palaces in the land of the Byzantines — and I was given the good news that my community would possess that. And the third time I looked toward Ṣanʿāʾ of Yemen; and all of these my community will possess.⟩ The hypocrites said: ⟨He fills you with hopes and promises you lies. This is the one who is in dread⟩ that is, who fears ⟨his enemies, to the point of digging the trench. We cannot relieve ourselves⟩ that is, go out for a person’s need ⟨and he promises you that you will possess the lands of Persia and of the Byzantines and the cities of Khusraw. There is no way to possessing these.⟩ So there was revealed: «Say» O Muhammad Allahumma O Allah «Owner of sovereignty, You give» You bestow «sovereignty to whom You will» of Your creation «and You strip sovereignty from whom You will»

— of them — «and You honour whom You will» — by giving him sovereignty — «and You abase whom You will» — by taking it away from him — «In Your hand» — by Your power — «is the good» — and the evil — «You are powerful over all things» (Q. 3:26). «You cause the night to pass into» — You bring the night into — «the day» (Q. 3:27). The night is twelve hours, and the day likewise. At certain times Allah, Blessed and Exalted, takes three hours from the night and puts them into the day, so the day becomes fifteen hours and the night nine hours; and at times
⟨he arose with his belly bound with a stone, and we remained three days without tasting any food⟩ ... [to the end of] the hadith.

it reverts until equality is reached. And He takes three hours from the day, so the night becomes fifteen hours and the day nine hours. He who is able to do this is able to give the community of Muhammad possession of the cities of Kisrā and of Ṣanʿāʾ of the Yemen. «and You cause the day to pass into the night, and You bring forth the living from the dead» — as the human being and the bird from the drop of seed and from the egg — «and You bring forth the dead» — as the drop of seed and the egg — «from the living, and You provide for whom You will without reckoning» (Q. 3:27) — ample provision. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the Possessor of sovereignty: He gives to whom He will, as He will. What the Prophet ﷺ gave glad tidings of came to pass, and they subdued the two great states. As for the first, which is the state of Persia — and it was the greatest state in the world — they shattered it until it became nothing, and the Muslims have ruled in it down to this day of ours. As for the second state, the Muslims stripped it of all its colonies, so that it remained a small state, and the Muslims gained mastery over them, until the state of the Muslims entered into Europe. Allah is the Possessor of sovereignty; He gives sovereignty to whom He will. When He is pleased with the creation — when they obey Him — He sets the righteous in authority among them, the masters of mercy and compassion; and when they disobey Him, He sets in authority the basest of the people and the worst of them, as the hadith indicates: ⟨As you are, so will you be governed.⟩ [16]

Mūsā, upon him be blessing and peace, said: ⟨My Lord, You are in heaven and we are on earth. How are we to know when You are pleased with us and when You are angry with us?⟩ He said: ⟨When I set the best of you in authority over you, know that I am pleased with you; and when I set the worst of you in authority, that is a sign of My anger.⟩ al-Ḥajjāj b. Yūsuf was an unjust king, a shedder of blood, who killed a hundred and seventy thousand Muslims. The scholars of his time addressed him; they said to him: “Fear Allah and act justly, like ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, for you lived to see the caliphate of ʿUmar. How is it that you are not like ʿUmar?” He said to them: tabadhdharū ataʿammar lakum — that is, be like Abū Dharr in renunciation and worship and I will be like ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb. This is how the saying of the Messenger ﷺ is to be construed: ⟨As you are, so will you be governed.⟩ The order of kingship is that upon which the subsistence of things rests. When he deals justly

the king, blessing descends upon crops and livestock and upon trade, so wealth becomes abundant; and when wealth becomes abundant the men grow strong, and when the men grow strong the state grows strong and the king grows strong. And when the king acts unjustly, blessing is lifted from crops and livestock, trade slumps, and the people become poor; and when the people become poor the men grow weak, and when the men grow weak there grows weak

the state, and the king grows weak. All of it is tied to the king’s justice and his injustice. One king among the kings of this world: his anger brings about the ruin of the world [entire] — what then of the anger of the King of kings, who is Allah, Blessed and Exalted? May Allah protect us from it. When ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz came to power, a scholar admonished him and said to him: “If you want to do good, appoint good men to office.” He said: ⟨That is admonition enough: when I appoint good men, they do good.⟩ There was a king among the kings who went out into the wilderness to hunt. He was cut off from his company and lost his way in the wilderness, and thirst overtook him. He came to a man who had an orchard and said to him: “Give me something from your orchard.” The man gave him a fruit; he split it open and drank, and found abundant sweet water in the fruit. The orchard pleased him, and he resolved in his heart to take the orchard by force. He said: “Hand me another fruit.” The man handed him another; he split it open and found it dry, with not a drop of water in it, sour. He said: “Glory be to Allah, what is this?” The man said: “Perhaps the king will review his intention. Did you intend something?” He remembered that he had intended to take the orchard by force, and the orchard’s condition had changed on the spot; and when he resolved on repentance, it reverted, and the fruits reverted to their [former] state. [17] All good lies in uprightness and all evil in crookedness. «He brings the living out of the dead» (Q. 3:27) In it there is a further interpretation: You bring forth the living

— the Muslim — out of the dead — out of the unbeliever. [18] An unbeliever begets a Muslim. You bring forth the living — the learned man — out of the dead — out of the ignorant man: you find an ignorant man who begets a child and the child turns out to be a scholar, and the reverse. Or: You bring forth the living — the living heart — out of the dead — out of the dead soul; when the soul dies, the heart comes alive. «And You bring the dead out of the living» (Q. 3:27) And when the soul comes alive, the heart dies. These are four verses. The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, Āyat al-Kursī, and two verses from [Āl ʿImrān]:⟩ «Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those who possess knowledge, upholding justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise. The religion with Allah is Islam» (Q. 3:18–19) and «Say: O Allah, Master of the kingdom» — to — «without reckoning» (Q. 3:26–27) Four verses which were suspended, with no veil between them and Allah. When He commanded that they be sent down to the earth, these four verses complained: “O Lord, do not send us down to one who disobeys You; we have no power to dwell beside one who disobeys You.” Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ⟨By My might and My majesty and the loftiness of My place, no human being recites you after every prayer but that Paradise becomes due to him, and but that I look upon him seventy times, in each look granting him seventy needs, the least of which is forgiveness.⟩ So they were content and came down. [19] They are four verses: Fātiḥat al-Kitāb , Āyat al-Kursī , Shahida Allah , and Qul Allahumma

Mālik al-Mulk . Whoever keeps constantly to reciting them has what has been mentioned. «Let not the believers take the unbelievers as allies» — allying with them and befriending them — [illegible: ص ذوب النومنين] do not abandon the believers and befriend the unbelievers — «And whoever does that»
[illegible: بواهم] «then he is not of Allah in anything» — then he is not of the religion of Allah in anything — «unless you take precaution against them as a precaution» (Q. 3:28) except

that you fear them with a fear. If the unbeliever has power and you fear him, you have a dispensation to ally with him outwardly, not inwardly; and the firm course is enmity toward the enemies of Allah and alliance with the friends of Allah. As for allying with the tongue and not with the heart, there is a dispensation for that; as for allying with the heart, there is no way to it. And the firm course is not to ally at all, even with the tongue. ⟨Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest [degree] of faith.⟩ [20]

«And He warns you» [means] makes you fear, «Allah, of Himself» that He will be angry with you if you take them as allies, «and to Allah is the destination» (Q. 3:28) and the destination is to Allah, the place of return to Him, and He will requite you. Strange: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, warns us and we do not fear Him, while man is weak in himself. He cannot bear a policeman’s slap, nor the heat of the sun, nor an ant’s sting; how can he withstand the wrath of the Lord and His punishment, and the Fire and the snakes and scorpions in it? [21]
…[is] able. Three things screen a person from disobedience, if he reflects: he reflects on the wrath of Allah, Blessed

[illegible: المكتونة] ⟨…every day seventy glances; and I fulfil for him every day seventy needs, the least of which is forgiveness; and I shield him from every enemy and give him victory over it; and nothing bars him from entering the Garden but that he should die.⟩ al-Suyūṭī gives it in the Musnad of ʿAli in al-Jāmiʿ al-Kabīr 99/2, in another transmission.

and Exalted, and on the severity of His punishment; and he reflects on his own weakness. When a person reflects on these things he will surely leave off contravening Allah, Blessed and Exalted. «Say» to them, «if you conceal what is in your breasts» [that is] your hearts, of alliance with them, «or reveal it» make it manifest, «Allah knows it» nothing is hidden from Him, «and» — that is, He — «He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is Powerful over everything» (Q. 3:29) and of that is the punishment of whoever allies himself with the unbelievers. Recall «the Day when every soul will find what it has done» [that is] what it has done, «of good, present before it, and what it has done» it, «of evil, it will wish that between itself and it there were a far-distant span» a limit at the furthest extremity of distance, so that it never reaches it, «and Allah warns you of Himself» He repeated it for emphasis, «and Allah is Compassionate toward the servants» (Q. 3:30) Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is intensely compassionate toward His servants. «the Day when every soul will find what it has done of good, present before it» (Q. 3:30) That is: when a person’s days are spent, the angel comes to him and takes his soul, and he is carried to the grave and buried. He finds a figure of repellent appearance and foul smell. He says to him: ⟨Get away from me; I do not want to see you.⟩ It says: ⟨I am your evil deed. How long you rode me, and today I shall ride you.⟩ And if he was a righteous servant of Allah, when he enters his grave he finds something beautiful. He says to it: ⟨Come near me — how fine your face, how sweet your scent.⟩ It says: ⟨I am your righteous deed. How long I rode you; so today you will ride me.⟩ [22] This is His words, Exalted: «the Day when every soul will find what it has done of good, present before it» in his grave «and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and it there were a far-distant span» (Q. 3:30) It was revealed when they said: ⟨We worship the idols only out of love for Allah, that they may bring us near to Him.⟩ As for the Jews and the delegation of Najrān, the Prophet ﷺ addressed them. He said to them: ⟨Submit.⟩ They said: ⟨We have submitted. We submitted before you; our religion precedes your religion and our Book precedes your Book.⟩ The Prophet ﷺ said to them: ⟨No. What bars you from Islam is that you say ʿĪsā is a son to Allah, and Allah has no child.⟩ They said to him: ⟨Which religion do you follow?⟩ He said: ⟨The religion of Ibrāhīm.⟩ They said: ⟨Ibrāhīm was a Jew.⟩ Allah, Blessed and Exalted, declared them liars: «Say» to them, O Muhammad

«If you love Allah, then follow me, Allah will love you» in the sense that He will reward you, «and He will forgive you your sins, and Allah is Forgiving» to whoever follows me, for what has passed from him before that, «Merciful» to him. (Q. 3:31) This proves that whoever loves Allah takes the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as his model. The sign of love for Allah is obedience to His Messenger ﷺ. Allah joined obedience to Himself with obedience to His Messenger: «Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah» (Q. 4:80) and He made the sign of love for Him obedience to the Messenger ﷺ. This is plain: whoever loves a person loves all those he loves and all who are attached to him. Whoever loves a beloved loves those of mankind who consort with him. Majnūn Laylā: when his love for Laylā grew intense he saw a dog in the open desert and clothed it in a garment; when he was challenged about this he said: ⟨My eye saw it once in Laylā’s quarter.⟩ [23] So whoever loves Allah — Allah’s beloved is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. «If you love Allah, then follow me, Allah will love you» (Q. 3:31) Whoever loves Allah, let him follow the Messenger ﷺ. Whoever claims love for Allah while abandoning the way of the Prophet ﷺ is a lying claimant.
Had your love been true you would have obeyed Him; the lover is obedient to the one he loves.

Following the Prophet ﷺ in all words and deeds is the highest means the servant takes for reaching the presence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. In the Qurʾan there are seven parties who followed seven things. Among them is one who obeyed his own soul: «His soul prompted him to the killing of his brother, so he killed him, and he became one of the losers» (Q. 5:30) We understood from this that nothing is born of following the soul except loss and regret. «and he followed his whim, so his likeness is the likeness of the dog: if you drive at it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants» (Q. 7:176) This is Balʿām: when he followed his whim he clung to the earth and followed his whim, so Allah transformed him and he became like the dog. And those who followed the chiefs of misguidance: «when those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment» (Q. 2:166) From this following nothing came out but regrets. Among them is one who followed Pharaoh: «they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right-guiding. He goes before his people on the Day of Resurrection and brings them down into the Fire — and an evil watering-place is that to which they are brought down» (Q. 11:97–98) Following Pharaoh has no result except entering the Fire, nothing else. Among them is one who followed the appetites: «then after them there succeeded successors who squandered the prayer and followed the appetites; so they will meet with ruin» (Q. 19:59)

And among them is the one who followed Iblīs; Allah promised him that he and whoever follows him: «I shall surely fill Hell with you and with those of them who follow you, all together» (Q. 38:85) «And Hell is indeed their appointed place, all together» (Q. 15:43) Iblīs and whoever follows him — their destination is Hell. There is no profit in following, except in following the Prophet ﷺ: «Say: If you love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and will forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful» (Q. 3:31) Whoever follows the Prophet ﷺ finds Allah’s love; and when Allah loves His servant, he becomes
⟨You disobey the Divinity while you display love for Him — this, by my life, is a marvel in reasoning. If your love were truthful you would have obeyed Him.⟩
⟨The lover is obedient to the one he loves. Every day He opens upon you with a blessing⟩
⟨from Him, while you squander the thanks for it.⟩

«the disbelievers» (Q. 3:32) He does not love them «Allah has chosen» selected «Ādam and Nūḥ and the family of Ibrāhīm» (Q. 3:33) Ibrāhīm [himself] «and the family of»

«ʿImrān» that is, ʿImrān «above the worlds» the worlds of their own age. (Q. 3:33) All of these Allah chose. He chose Ādam and made him a vicegerent on the earth, and He sent Nūḥ, who is the first of the prophets of the shariʿa , and Ibrāhīm, the Friend of Allah, and ʿImrān — these Allah made prophets: «a progeny, some of them from others» (Q. 3:34) and these prophets Allah made a progeny, some of them from the offspring of others. «And Allah is Hearing, Knowing» (Q. 3:34) Nūḥ is of the progeny of Ādam, and Ibrāhīm of the progeny of Nūḥ, and Ibrāhīm fathered Ismāʿīl and Isḥāq. Isḥāq is the father of Yaʿqūb, who is Isrāʾīl. The prophets of the Banū Isrāʾīl are all of them from Isḥāq, and the prophets of the Arabs, among whom is the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad ﷺ are of the progeny of Ismāʿīl. So the prophets were all of them a progeny, some of them from others, and that is the wisdom of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. ⟨The child is the secret of his father.⟩ [n. 26] And for this reason you find most often that the prophets are the sons of prophets, the awliyāʾ the sons of the awliyāʾ , the scholars the sons of scholars, the kings the sons of kings, the disbelievers the sons of disbelievers, the transgressors the sons of transgressors. This is the rule, and it does not fail except for an accident: an accident may come, by the will of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and alter this pattern. That is because when the father is righteous and his intention is righteous, and he marries lawfully, and eats what is wholesome, and goes in to

his wife, and is granted a child, that child will be a believer and a walī , because of the goodness of his deed, the wholesomeness of his food, the goodness of his intention, and the soundness of his creed — unless an accident intervenes and corrupts the child.

And the father, when he is a disbeliever whose creed is bad and darkened and whose intention is bad, and he eats what is unlawful and marries unlawfully — when the child comes out, it comes out a disbeliever or a transgressor, unless an accident intervenes and purifies this child. For this reason the hadith has come down: ⟨The child is the secret of his father.⟩ This appears in ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace: he has no father, but the one who breathed into his mother so that she conceived was Jibrīl, upon him be blessing and peace. For that reason you find the states of the angels predominant in ʿĪsā
«a progeny, some of them from others. And Allah is Hearing, Knowing» (Q. 3:34) «when she said» recall when she said «the wife of ʿImrān» (Q. 3:35)

Ḥanna bint Fāqūdā [27]: when she had grown old and longed for a child, she prayed to Allah and felt herself with child. This Ḥanna, the mother of Maryam, was barren; she used to envy women their children and wished that she might find a child of her own. One day she looked at the servants of the mosque of Jerusalem and wished that, if she had a child, she would make him an offering, to be one of those servants in the mosque. So Allah granted her a pregnancy, and when she felt herself with child she said: «My Lord, I have vowed» that I shall make «to You what is in my womb dedicated» freed, kept pure from the preoccupations of this world, for the service of Your sanctified house «so accept from me; You are the Hearing» of supplication «the Knowing» of intentions (Q. 3:35). And ʿImrān died while she was still pregnant. «And when she gave birth to her» she bore her a girl, whereas she had been hoping it would be a boy, since only boys were dedicated. «She said» (Q. 3:36)

excusing herself: «My Lord, I have given birth to her, a female» I have borne the child a female «and Allah knew best what she had borne» a parenthetical clause «and the male is not» whom I asked for «like the female» that was bestowed on me (Q. 3:36). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knows best what she bore. «And the male is not like the female» admits two senses: the male whom I asked for is not like the female that You bestowed on me; the female is more deficient than the male, on account of her weakness, her ʿawra , and what befalls her of menstruation

and her oil, and he would find with her the fruit of summer in winter and the fruit of winter in summer [28]. These are the karāmāt of the saints, since she was not one of the prophets. Whoever denies the karāmāt of the saints has given the lie to two hundred verses and to more than five hundred hadith. For this Maryam — the fruit of winter used to be found with her in summer, and the fruit of summer in winter. She was raised in the sanctuary of the mosque, and no man ever saw her except Zakariyāʾ, her maḥram , who would come in to her with her water for purification, her drink, and her food. «Whenever Zakariyāʾ entered upon her in the sanctuary» the chamber «he found with her provision. He said: O Maryam, from where have you this?» the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter? «She said» — she was still a child — «It is from Allah» He brings it to me from the Garden «Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning» an ample provision with no liability (Q. 3:37). This is one of the karāmāt of the saints. And whoever denies the karāmāt of the saints — [sentence incomplete]. They said that this is an irhāṣ , a foretoken belonging to the miracles of ʿĪsā, the child. The karāmāt of the saints are established in the Book and the Sunna, and they have been witnessed; for that reason none can deny them but a flat denier. The fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter. A karāma like this one happened to Fāṭima, the daughter of the Messenger ﷺ. She had with her a small piece of meat and a piece of bread. She saw the hunger the Prophet ﷺ was suffering, and she preferred the Prophet ﷺ over herself; so she came and set it before the Prophet ﷺ. When the Prophet lifted the cover, the bowl was full of good meat and bread and fat. The Messenger ﷺ called her, and she looked. He said: ⟨From where have you this?⟩ She said: ⟨It is from Allah.⟩ He said: ⟨al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh (The Praise is for Allah), who has made you like Maryam the daughter of ʿImrān, the mistress of the women of her world.⟩ The people of the house ate [all of them], and some was left over; they fed the people of the Ṣuffa [the portico of the mosque], and some was left over; then he said that it be sent to every house in Medina, and it was not used up [29]. And stranger still than this: one day of

the days, al-Ḥasan longed for some food, so they sold Fāṭima’s shift for six dirhams and prepared food. When nothing was left but the eating, a poor man stopped [at the door] and asked them for alms, and they handed it to him. Then ʿAli went out and met a man selling a camel. He said to him: ⟨Sell me the camel.⟩ He said: ⟨I will sell it to you for six dirhams on credit.⟩ So ʿAli took the camel for six dirhams on credit. Then he met another man, who said to him: ⟨Sell me the camel.⟩ He said to him: ⟨How much will you give me?⟩ He said to him: ⟨Sixty-six dirhams.⟩ So he paid him sixty-six dirhams. He took the six dirhams, intending to settle the debt he had incurred, and he sought out the first seller but did not find him; so he came with sixty-six dirhams. The Messenger said to him: ⟨Do you know the seller? The first seller was Riḍwān, the keeper of the Garden; he is the one who advanced you the camel. And the one who bought it from you for sixty-six dirhams, that was Mīkāʾīl. And the first beggar, who tested you by taking your food, was Jibrīl. Jibrīl is⟩

⟨[I am] hungry.⟩ She said: ⟨No, by Allah — [may] my father and my mother [be your ransom].⟩ When he left her, a neighbour of hers sent her two loaves and a piece of meat. She took it from her and put it in a bowl of hers, and said: ⟨By Allah, I shall give the Messenger of Allah ﷺ preference in this over myself and over those with me.⟩ They were all of them in need of a full meal. So she sent al-Ḥasan, or al-Husayn, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he came back to her. ⟨So I brought him the bowl and uncovered it, and there it was, filled with bread and meat. When I looked at it I was dumbfounded, and I knew that it was a blessing from Allah. So I praised Allah and invoked blessing upon His Prophet, and I set it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he saw it he praised Allah and said: ‘From where have you this, O my daughter?’ She said: ‘O my father, it is from Allah; Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.’ So he praised Allah and said: ‘⟩ al-Ḥamdu li-Llāh ⟨(The Praise is for Allah), who has made you, O my daughter, the likeness of the mistress of the women of the Children of Israel; for when Allah provided her with something and she was asked about it, she would say: It is from Allah; Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.’ Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for ʿAli; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate, and ʿAli ate, and Fāṭima, and Ḥasan, and Husayn, and all the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and the people of his house, until all of them were filled. The poor man, and the first seller, was Riḍwān, the keeper of the Garden; and the buyer was Mīkāʾīl, inasmuch as he found sixty-six dirhams in place of six dirhams. [30] 1.

When Zakariyyāʾ considered Maryam’s condition, he knew that the One able to bring this at this season is able to grant a child in old age. «There Zakariyyāʾ called upon his Lord» when he entered the sanctuary at night, to pray in the dead of night «He said: My Lord, grant me from You» from Your presence «a goodly offspring» a righteous child «You are the Hearer of supplication. Then the angels called to him» (Q. 3:38) that is, Jibrīl «while he was standing praying in the sanctuary» in the place of worship «that Allah gives you good news of Yaḥyā, confirming a word from Allah» the word is ʿĪsā, upon him be blessing and peace; they were maternal cousins «and a chief» one who is followed «and chaste» kept back from women — not from incapacity, but he withheld himself «and a prophet from among the righteous» (Q. 3:39) «He said: My Lord, how shall I have a boy» a son «when old age has overtaken me» that is, I have reached the limit of age, a hundred and twenty years «and my wife is barren» she had reached ninety-eight years «He said» the matter «is thus» (Q. 3:40)

that Allah create a boy from the two of you «Allah does what He wills» (Q. 3:40) nothing defeats Him He speaks here of doing, and in the case of ʿĪsā of creating, because the case of ʿĪsā breaks the customary order more severely: this is doing, that is creating. «He said: My Lord, appoint for me a sign» a mark of my wife’s pregnancy «He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people» you will be kept from speaking to them, [occupied] with the remembrance of Allah «for three days» this is the basis of the three-day retreat that the righteous undertake «except by sign» a gesture «and remember your Lord much, and glorify» pray «in the evening and the early morning» (Q. 3:41) [and] recall «when the angels said: Maryam, Allah has chosen you» selected you «and purified you» from men’s touch «and chosen you above the women of the worlds» (Q. 3:42) the people of your time meaning the world of her own time The Messenger ﷺ said: ⟨There have attained perfection among men⟩

⟨many, and of women none has reached perfection except a few: Maryam the daughter of ʿImrān, and Āsiya the daughter of Muzāḥim⟩ [32] ⟨, and Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid, and ʿAʾisha the daughter of Abū Bakr, and Fāṭima the daughter of Muhammad ﷺ.⟩ [33] 2. Of them the poet says:
